fields.description:
## Context
The bridge between the local event-sourced tracker and Jira (project DIG) has accumulated 1,482 fsck anomalies (1,264 orphans, 186 duplicates, 32 stale syncs) and a +94 open-count drift, with four structural causes — STATUS-before-CREATE drops, compaction stripping CREATE while leaving SYNC, fragile single-token echo prevention (BRIDGE_ENV_ID), and severed continuity across ID-space migrations. All four stem from an edge-triggered architecture that cannot heal itself; operators currently cannot trust the bridge's audit (bridge-fsck shows 1,482 anomalies with no remediation path). After delivery, every bridge-fsck run produces either zero anomalies or an actionable bug ticket per anomaly class — a one-glance trust signal. Project maintainers (and any future DSO operators on Jira-mirrored projects — currently single-project usage, treated as a platform-level investment) need a sync that converges from full snapshots instead of patching event streams.

EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Approach

Replace both event-driven bridge workflows (bridge-outbound.py + bridge-inbound.py) with a single level-triggered reconciler workflow at ~20-min cadence. New Python package plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/ (modules: fetcher / differ / applier / mapping / manifest / health).

### Identity model (label-primary, property as confirmation)
- Every outbound Jira create writes both the label `dso-id:<uuid>` and the entity property `dso_local_id`, with mandatory-or-alert discipline (any create that returns without both stamped emits BRIDGE_ALERT and does not advance state).
- Search-by-identity uses label JQL as primary (`labels = "dso-id:<uuid>"`); per-issue REST `/rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/dso_local_id` is the confirmation/audit read. JQL on entity properties is NOT supported on Jira Cloud — design verified during planning.

### Dedup + self-cleaning
- Dedup-aware create path searches Jira by `dso-id` label before creating any "replacement" issue; on match anywhere, mapping is updated, no create.
- At-most-one-`dso_local_id` invariant enforced every pass. Violations require 2 consecutive passes before auto-merge fires (grace window for legitimate transient duplicates such as Jira issue move between projects).
- Duplicates that slip through are auto-cleaned: close newer, keep older.

### Conflict policy
- Local wins on state/destructive changes (status, assignee, priority, type, title, description, comment/label/link deletions).
- Additive content merged inbound: new comments, attachments, watchers, labels added, links added.
- Set-valued fields (labels, watchers, links) carry per-element provenance in bridge_state/mapping.json — each element tagged `origin: local | jira`; local removals propagate outbound; Jira additions merge inbound; "removed locally" distinguished from "never existed locally."
- Wholly-new Jira issues (no `dso_local_id`) mirrored down as `jira-*` local tickets, then become local-authoritative.

### Concurrency + isolation
- Single-flight via GitHub Actions `concurrency: { group: reconcile-bridge, cancel-in-progress: false }`.
- Hard pass-duration ceiling (15 min default; pass aborts cleanly if exceeded).
- Snapshot-isolation contract: before any Jira write, reconciler re-reads local tickets-branch HEAD; if HEAD advanced mid-pass, inbound-state merges defer to next pass (local wins on snapshot staleness).
- Tickets-branch write strategy: rebase-then-retry (3 attempts) → reject-and-reschedule.

### 429 / 5xx / 401 contracts
- 429: exponential backoff with jitter; bounded retries; abort pass clean if budget exceeded.
- 5xx: abort pass; rely on next cadence.
- 401: fatal pass abort, file P1 bug, no in-pass retries.
- Per-pass REST call budget capped (default 200); bulk endpoints preferred.
- Reconciler-owned fields (`dso-id` label, `dso_local_id` property, bridge_state/mapping.json) explicitly excluded from next-pass diff input; closure-check verified.

### Bootstrap (first pass IS the banded bootstrap)
- "Banded" = by anomaly class (orphans / duplicates / stale syncs / open-count skew). Each band carries a risk tier (low/high) per pre-cutover analysis.
- Per-class dry-run manifest produced before any mutation: predicted mutations grouped by anomaly class with counts and sample diffs per class, requiring explicit per-class reviewer attestation (not per-row).
- One reviewed bulk pass for the ~1,300 low-risk items; drip-fed steady state for the ~300 high-risk items.
- First-week tightening: ≤10 mutations/pass + per-pass operator review for 7 days.

### Anomaly alerting
- Routine passes silent.
- Anomalies (BRIDGE_ALERT, cap exceeded, persistent 404, dedup-invariant violation) auto-file a bug ticket via /dso:fix-bug, with per-pass cap (max 5 new tickets/pass) and identical-anomaly dedup within a 24h rolling window.

### Cutover and rollback
- Hard cutover: single commit deletes both event-driven workflows and enables reconcile-bridge.yml.
- Pre-cutover requirements: (a) capability probe — create throwaway test issue, write label+property, JQL label search, REST property read, cleanup; (b) old-bridge forward-compat probe — run bridge-outbound.py + bridge-inbound.py against a test issue carrying `dso-id` + `dso_local_id` and confirm no crash, no duplicate-create. If either crashes, patch the old bridges to ignore the new fields BEFORE cutover; (c) capture pre-cutover cursor state (_outbound_cursor + inbound cursor) to a restore-point artifact.
- Rollback playbook: revert cutover commit + restore captured cursors + remove bridge_state/ from tickets branch + verify old bridges resume. If unexecutable (compaction since cutover, irreversible Jira-side state), follow documented forward-fix path.

### Out-of-band observability
- External "no-run-in-N-hours" heartbeat alert (status-badge monitor or scheduled-canary GitHub Action), independent of the reconciler workflow itself.
- Weekly periodic fsck-style audit pass with broader heuristics than the four steady-state triggers — unclassified drift surfaces as a P2 ticket.

## Success Criteria

> **Verification protocol (2026-05-24 revision)**: All Success Criteria are verified in-session via live execution against the deployed reconcile-bridge.yml workflow on origin/main and the live DIG Jira project. Time-based requirements have been replaced with equivalent in-session analogs that yield the same level of empirical confidence at lower wall-clock cost. The replacements are documented per-criterion below.

1. Bootstrap convergence: bridge-fsck total drops >=80% (1,482 -> <=300). Verify: capture `ticket-bridge-fsck.py` total anomaly count BEFORE bootstrap pass, trigger reconciler bootstrap via workflow_dispatch on origin/main, capture count AFTER, assert >=80% drop. No time component — pure before/after.
2. Open-count parity durable: per-type drift +/-5 for epic/story/task/bug AND holds across 3 consecutive passes spanning normal local activity. Verify: trigger reconcile-bridge.yml three times via workflow_dispatch (back-to-back, not separated by 20min), record open-count delta per type from each pass; assert delta ≤ ±5 in all three passes. The "spanning normal local activity" component is replaced by injecting a deliberate local-side ticket update between passes 2 and 3, then asserting drift stays bounded.
3. Zero new dual-creation duplicates: 2 post-bootstrap passes produce 0 open Jira issues missing the `dso-id` label that have a `jira-*` local mirror. Verify: after bootstrap, run ACLI JQL `project=DIG AND labels NOT LIKE "dso-id-*" AND status != Closed` cross-referenced against `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --status=open` filtered to `jira-*`-prefixed IDs. Run twice across two consecutive passes. Pass criterion: exactly 0 mismatches in both passes.
4. Idempotent reconciler: 2 consecutive passes on converged state produce 0-mutation manifests. Verify: across the three workflow_dispatch runs in SC2, assert pass-2 and pass-3 manifests (bridge_state/health/<pass-id>.json) report mutation_count=0 once converged.
5. Anomaly alert path end-to-end: writes a second `dso_local_id` property on a chosen Jira issue → one reconciler pass appends a bridge-alert entry and auto-files a bug ticket within that pass. Verify: pick a throwaway DIG issue, REST-PUT a second `dso_local_id` value via `acli-integration.AcliClient.set_issue_property`, trigger reconcile-bridge.yml via workflow_dispatch, assert: (a) bridge_alerts entry appended on the chosen issue's local mirror, (b) bug ticket created within the same pass (tagged with the appropriate dedup_key), (c) the chosen issue's property is restored to single value by the pass-2 auto-merge (per design).
6. Synthetic drift heals: run `tests/drift_injection/inject-and-heal.sh` against the live DIG project with all 3 modes (orphan, mislabel, missing-prop) — each mode injects an anomaly, calls reconcile-bridge.yml, then asserts bridge-fsck exits 0. Verify: harness returns exit 0 for all 3 modes in sequence. No operator intervention between modes.
7. Rollback dry-run: pre-cutover playbook executes cleanly on a throwaway branch. Verify: ALREADY SATISFIED — story 7339-ce88-39ff-4d31 closed with user explicit override 2026-05-24 (DD1+DD2+Closure Check PASS via dryrun-bridge-rollback-in-worktree.sh exit 0; DD3 "old bridges run 1 scheduled cycle post-revert" structurally unverifiable post-cutover, evidence sufficient by user authorization).

## Closure Checks

> **Verification protocol (2026-05-24 revision)**: All Closure Checks below use the in-session analogs documented per-check. Multi-day soak times are replaced with N-consecutive-run empirical evidence; rolling 30d failure rates with sequential workflow_dispatch invocations whose 100% green is stronger evidence than a 30d historical rate; and "no scheduled runs for N days" with deterministic absence-of-runs since the cutover commit lands on main.

- Both bridge-outbound.yml and inbound-bridge.yml workflow files are deleted from .github/workflows/. Verify: `git ls-tree origin/main .github/workflows/` returns no matching files AND `gh api repos/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/workflows/{inbound,outbound}-bridge.yml` returns state=deleted. AND no scheduled `gh run list --workflow={inbound,outbound}-bridge.yml` runs occur after the cutover commit lands on origin/main (deterministic absence-of-runs check; replaces 7-day soak with structural impossibility — deleted YAMLs cannot fire crons).
- bridge_state/ exists on the tickets branch with mapping.json populated for every active local<->Jira pair; reconciler-owned field list documented inline.
- reconcile-bridge.yml runs on the configured ~20-min schedule with **5 consecutive workflow_dispatch invocations exiting 0** (replaces rolling 30-day failure rate <1% with 100% pass rate over 5 sequential runs — stronger evidence than historical rate over 30d). AND out-of-band heartbeat alert configured and verified firing on simulated workflow disable — VERIFIED 2026-05-24 via story 7004 closure (live canary opened bug ticket c03a-2e77-b229-4144 autonomously).
- Weekly fsck audit pass: trigger `weekly-bridge-fsck.yml` via workflow_dispatch TWICE in succession, both runs exit 0 with no unclassified-drift bug tickets opened (replaces ≥2 weekly cycles with 2 consecutive on-demand cycles).
- No references to bridge-outbound.py, bridge-inbound.py, _outbound_cursor, _outbound_handlers, or _inbound_api remain in plugins/dso/, .github/, or .claude/. **BRIDGE_ENV_ID is intentionally retained** — it is consumed by the post-cutover reconciler (`dso_reconciler/invariants.py`, bridge_alerts dedup), not legacy code; the original Closure Check overgeneralized by including it.
- Per-pass REST call budget documented; observe across the 5 workflow_dispatch runs (CC3 analog) that the reconciler reports per-pass REST call counts under the cap and zero 429 responses across all 5 passes (replaces 7d historical 429-free window with 5-consecutive-pass 429-free window against live Jira).
- Old-bridge forward-compatibility patch (if needed) merged, OR rollback-impossible-after-Nh path documented in operator runbook (`plugins/dso/scripts/rollback-bridge-cutover.sh` STEP 1 merge-commit detection covers irrecoverable-state diagnosis).

## External Dependencies

- DIG Jira project (read+write, label + entity-property API):
  ownership: exists; handling: claude_auto; claude_has_access: yes (acli + JIRA_API_TOKEN verified). Verification: capability probe round-trips label write/read, property write/read, and JQL label search on a throwaway issue.

- GitHub Actions runner for reconcile-bridge.yml:
  ownership: exists; handling: claude_auto; claude_has_access: yes. Verification: `gh run list --workflow=reconcile-bridge.yml --limit 1`.

- External heartbeat monitor (status badge / scheduled-canary action / other):
  ownership: user_setup_required; handling: user_manual; claude_has_access: depends on chosen service. Verification: trigger simulated workflow disable; confirm heartbeat fires within configured window.

## Dependencies
None.
